title: Domain 1 extra questions (1.1-1.4)
note: Original questions written for IdentityOps Lab. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks.

questions.stem: After a string of break-ins, a company installs a tall perimeter fence with a locked gate around its equipment yard. Which of the following control categories does the fence belong to?
questions.explanation: A fence is a tangible barrier that restricts access to a space, so it is a physical control. It is not operational, because operational controls are activities carried out by people, such as guard patrols or training.

questions.stem: Which of the following control categories describes security activities that are carried out mainly by people day to day, such as staff following an incident response procedure or administrators reviewing logs each morning?
questions.explanation: Operational controls are procedures that people perform as part of daily operations. Managerial controls are tempting, but they focus on oversight and planning, such as policies and risk assessments, rather than the hands-on work.

questions.stem: A security manager writes a vendor risk management program that defines how suppliers are evaluated and approved before any contract is signed. Which of the following control categories BEST describes this program?
questions.explanation: A program that sets how risk is evaluated and governed is a managerial (administrative) control. The evaluations staff later carry out could be operational, but the program itself is a management decision about how risk is handled.

questions.stem: A cloud administrator enables encryption on all storage buckets and configures security groups so that only the web tier can reach the database tier. Which of the following control categories do these settings represent?
questions.explanation: Encryption and security group rules are enforced by systems, which makes them technical controls. They are not operational, because no person has to perform an activity for them to take effect.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a technical control?
questions.explanation: A firewall rule is enforced by technology, so it is a technical control. A locked cabinet also restricts access but does so with a physical barrier, which makes it a physical control.

questions.stem: After several thefts, a warehouse installs bright floodlights and highly visible cameras around its loading docks. The main goal is to make would-be thieves decide the target is not worth the risk. Which of the following control types BEST describes the lighting?
questions.explanation: Lighting that makes intruders feel exposed discourages them from trying, which is a deterrent control. It does not detect anything on its own; a camera recording footage would be the detective element.

questions.stem: A web application firewall is set to blocking mode and drops any request that matches a known attack signature before the request reaches the web server. Which of the following control types does this represent?
questions.explanation: Dropping the malicious request stops the attack before it can succeed, which is a preventive control. If the firewall only logged or alerted on the request, it would be detective instead.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the difference between a preventive control and a deterrent control?
choices: A preventive control records an action; a deterrent blocks it
A preventive control is always technical; a deterrent is always physical
A preventive control stops an action; a deterrent only discourages it
A preventive control repairs damage; a deterrent identifies it
questions.answer: A preventive control stops an action; a deterrent only discourages it
questions.explanation: A preventive control physically or logically blocks the action, while a deterrent tries to change the attacker's mind. Both can be technical or physical, so the category option is wrong.

questions.stem: A small business places stickers from a well-known alarm monitoring company on its front windows, even though the alarm system covers only the back office. Which of the following control types do the stickers represent?
questions.explanation: The stickers aim to discourage burglars from attempting a break-in, which makes them deterrent. The alarm system itself would be detective, but the stickers detect nothing.

questions.stem: To stop employees from installing unapproved software, the IT department removes local administrator rights from all standard user accounts. Which of the following control types BEST describes this change?
questions.explanation: Without administrator rights, users are technically unable to install software, so the control prevents the action. A directive control would only tell users not to install software without enforcing it.

questions.stem: A SIEM correlates authentication logs and raises an alert when the same account signs in from two different countries within ten minutes. Which of the following control types does the alert represent?
questions.explanation: The SIEM identifies and reports suspicious activity after it occurs, which is a detective control. It is not preventive, because the sign-ins are allowed to happen; the alert only reveals them.

questions.stem: After an employee falls for a phishing email, an administrator resets the employee's password and revokes all active sessions for the account. Which of the following control types BEST describes these actions?
questions.explanation: Resetting the password and revoking sessions fixes the problem after the incident has happened, which makes them corrective. They do block further misuse, but their purpose here is to repair the damage of a compromise already detected.

questions.stem: A file integrity monitoring tool sends an alert reporting that a system binary on a web server changed outside of any approved maintenance. Which of the following control types is the monitoring tool?
questions.explanation: File integrity monitoring discovers unexpected changes and reports them, which is detective. It is not corrective, because it does not restore the original file.

questions.stem: Endpoint protection software finds malware on a laptop, removes it, and rolls back the registry changes the malware made. Which of the following control types BEST describes the removal and rollback?
questions.explanation: Removing the malware and undoing its changes returns the system to a good state, which is a corrective control. The software did detect the malware first, but the question asks about the cleanup action, not the discovery.

questions.stem: Which of the following control types has the main purpose of identifying and recording that a security event has occurred?
questions.explanation: Detective controls, such as logs, alarms and intrusion detection, reveal that something happened. Corrective controls act after detection to repair or restore, so they are a different stage.

questions.stem: A two-person finance office cannot separate the duties of approving and issuing payments. Instead, the owner reviews every payment at the end of each month. In this situation, which of the following control types BEST describes the owner's review?
questions.explanation: The review is used because the required control, separation of duties, cannot be implemented, so it is a compensating control. A review does reveal problems like a detective control, but its role here is to stand in for the missing primary control.

questions.stem: Every new employee must sign an acceptable use policy stating that personal cloud storage services must not be used for company files. No software blocks those services. Which of the following control types is this policy?
questions.explanation: The policy tells people what they are expected to do without enforcing it, which is a directive control. It is not preventive, because nothing technically stops an employee from using the services.

questions.stem: Which of the following control types is used when a required primary control cannot be implemented, providing an alternative safeguard that reduces the same risk?
questions.explanation: A compensating control is a substitute for a control that is not feasible. Corrective controls fix problems after an incident occurs, which is a different purpose.

questions.stem: A vendor will not release a patch for a critical server vulnerability until next month. In the meantime, the team disables the vulnerable feature and adds an intrusion prevention signature for the exploit. Which of the following control types do these temporary measures represent?
questions.explanation: The measures stand in for the patch, which cannot be applied yet, so they are compensating controls. Patching would be the corrective action; these are the alternative safeguards used until it is possible.

questions.stem: During onboarding, new hires receive a written procedure instructing them to report suspicious emails by using the report button in their mail client. Which of the following control types does this procedure represent?
questions.explanation: A written instruction that guides how people should act is a directive control. The reports staff send may help detect phishing, but the procedure itself directs behavior rather than detecting anything.

questions.stem: A hospital deploys redundant power supplies and a failover database cluster so that clinicians can still open patient records if a server fails. Which of the following security principles is the hospital MOST directly supporting?
questions.explanation: Redundancy and failover keep the records reachable when something breaks, which supports availability. Integrity is about preventing unauthorized changes to the data, which these measures do not address.

questions.stem: A company encrypts its payroll database so that storage administrators who manage the underlying disks cannot read employees' salary information. Which of the following principles does this PRIMARILY protect?
questions.explanation: Encryption keeps the data unreadable to people who are not authorized to see it, which protects confidentiality. It does not by itself stop someone from altering or deleting data, so integrity is not the main goal.

questions.stem: An attacker on the network path intercepts a wire transfer request and changes the destination account number before it reaches the bank. Which of the following security principles has been violated?
questions.explanation: Changing the content of the request is an unauthorized modification, which violates integrity. Confidentiality would be violated if the attacker only read the request without changing it.

questions.stem: A legal team needs proof that a specific manager sent an email, so that the manager cannot later deny sending it. Which of the following BEST provides this assurance?
choices: Encryption with a shared symmetric key
A hash of the message body
questions.explanation: A digital signature is created with the sender's private key, which only the sender holds, so it provides non-repudiation. A shared symmetric key does not work, because both parties hold the same key and either could have produced the message.

questions.stem: After a user signs in successfully, the file server checks the user's group memberships to decide whether the user may open the finance share. Which of the following AAA functions is the server performing?
questions.explanation: Deciding what an already verified user is allowed to access is authorization. Authentication happened earlier, when the user proved their identity by signing in.

questions.stem: Two application servers call each other's APIs. Each server proves its identity with a certificate installed on it instead of a person's username and password. Which of the following does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: The identity being verified belongs to a machine, not a user, so this is system authentication. Authorization is tempting, but it decides what an identity may do after it has been authenticated.

questions.stem: A company grants access to the personnel folder based on job function, so everyone in the HR department automatically receives read access when they join the team. Which of the following authorization models is this?
questions.explanation: Granting permissions according to a person's job role is role-based access control. Rule-based access control applies conditions such as time of day or source address to everyone, rather than permissions tied to a role.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes authentication?
choices: Deciding which resources an identity may use
Proving that a claimed identity is genuine
Recording what an identity did during a session
Stating an identity by entering a username
questions.answer: Proving that a claimed identity is genuine
questions.explanation: Authentication verifies a claimed identity, for example with a password, token or biometric. Entering a username is only identification, the claim that authentication then checks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY output of a gap analysis?
choices: Exploitable vulnerabilities found on every network host
Differences between current and target security state
Business functions ranked by recovery priority
A history of changes made to production systems
questions.answer: Differences between current and target security state
questions.explanation: A gap analysis compares where the organization is with where it wants to be and lists the differences. Finding exploitable vulnerabilities is the job of a vulnerability scan or penetration test, not a gap analysis.

questions.stem: A security team has just finished a gap analysis against a recognized framework and found twelve missing controls. Which of the following should the team do NEXT?
choices: Repeat the analysis against another framework
Run a penetration test against each gap
Close the project because the assessment is done
Build a prioritized plan to close the gaps
questions.answer: Build a prioritized plan to close the gaps
questions.explanation: The value of a gap analysis comes from acting on it, so the next step is a prioritized remediation plan. Repeating the analysis against another framework would delay fixing the gaps already identified.

questions.stem: A company is about to begin a gap analysis of its security program. Which of the following must be defined FIRST?
choices: The baseline or framework to measure against
The list of owners for each remediation task
The budget for purchasing new controls
The scope of a future penetration test
questions.answer: The baseline or framework to measure against
questions.explanation: A gap can only be measured against a target, so the desired baseline or framework must be chosen first. Remediation owners and budgets come later, after the gaps are known.

questions.stem: A healthcare company acquires a small clinic. The CISO wants to compare the clinic's existing safeguards with the parent company's security standard to find out what the clinic is missing. Which of the following should the CISO perform?
questions.explanation: Comparing existing controls with a required standard to find what is missing is a gap analysis. A vulnerability assessment looks for technical weaknesses in systems, not missing controls measured against a standard.

questions.stem: A zero trust design gives each user access only to the specific applications they need and segments the network so that a compromised account can reach as few resources as possible. Which of the following concepts does this BEST illustrate?
questions.explanation: Limiting what any single identity can reach shrinks the area an attacker can affect, which is threat scope reduction. Adaptive identity is about adjusting authentication requirements based on context, not limiting reach.

questions.stem: In a zero trust architecture, which of the following describes the area behind the policy enforcement point, where a resource is located and traffic that has passed the enforcement point is allowed to reach it?
questions.explanation: The implicit trust zone is the area behind the policy enforcement point where the resource lives. The control plane holds the decision-making components, not the resources being protected.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the core principle of a zero trust model?
choices: Trust any device inside the corporate perimeter
Verify users only once when they join the VPN
Block all traffic that originates from outside networks
Verify every access request, wherever it comes from
questions.answer: Verify every access request, wherever it comes from
questions.explanation: Zero trust assumes no request is trusted by default and evaluates each one, whether it comes from inside or outside the network. Trusting devices inside the perimeter is the traditional model that zero trust replaces.

questions.stem: A museum wants an alarm to trigger when anyone steps onto a mat placed directly in front of a valuable display case. Which of the following sensor types should be used?
questions.explanation: A pressure sensor detects weight or force, such as a person stepping on a mat. Infrared sensors detect body heat in an area, which could trigger on visitors who never step in front of the case.

questions.stem: A facility needs motion sensors that send out signals and detect movement from their reflections over a large area, including through thin non-metal walls. Which of the following sensor types BEST meets this need?
questions.explanation: Microwave sensors emit microwave pulses, cover large areas and can pass through some non-metal materials. Ultrasonic sensors also use reflections, but sound waves do not pass through walls.

questions.stem: A data center's main gate must verify visitors' identities and also handle unusual situations, such as a delivery driver who arrives without paperwork. Which of the following controls is BEST suited to this?
questions.explanation: A security guard can check identity and use human judgment to handle exceptions. A badge reader can only accept or reject a badge and cannot deal with someone who has none.

questions.stem: Equipment was stolen from a loading dock last week, and management wants to find out who entered the area and when. Which of the following physical controls would BEST provide this information?
questions.explanation: Recorded video shows who entered the area and at what time, so it supports the investigation. Lighting helps deter intruders and improves visibility, but it records nothing on its own.

questions.stem: A security team sets up a single decoy server that appears to run an outdated, vulnerable FTP service so that it can observe the techniques attackers use. Which of the following has the team deployed?
questions.explanation: A single decoy system built to attract and observe attackers is a honeypot. A honeynet is a group of decoy systems working together, not one server.

questions.stem: A research team builds several decoy systems, including a web server, a database server and two workstations, all connected to look like a real department's network. Which of the following BEST describes this setup?
questions.explanation: A network of multiple decoy systems is a honeynet. A honeypot is a single decoy system, so it does not describe a whole connected environment.

questions.stem: An administrator places a spreadsheet named "admin passwords" on a file share. The file contains no real credentials, and opening it immediately alerts the security team. Which of the following is this spreadsheet?
questions.explanation: A decoy document that triggers an alert when opened is a honeyfile. A honeytoken is a fake piece of data, such as a credential or API key, that alerts when someone tries to use it rather than when a file is opened.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY benefit of deploying a honeypot on an internal network?
choices: Blocking malware before it reaches endpoints
Encrypting sensitive data stored on servers
Removing the need for an intrusion prevention system
Detecting attackers and learning their techniques
questions.answer: Detecting attackers and learning their techniques
questions.explanation: Legitimate users have no reason to touch a honeypot, so any activity on it reveals an attacker and shows how they operate. A honeypot does not block malware; it attracts and observes rather than prevents.

questions.stem: Which of the following change management elements identifies the person accountable for making sure a change is carried out and its results are verified?
questions.explanation: Ownership assigns a specific person who is accountable for the change. Stakeholders are the people affected by the change, but they are not necessarily responsible for delivering it.

questions.stem: A developer has finished a new feature and tested it in the staging environment. According to the company's change management process, which of the following must happen BEFORE the feature is deployed to production?
choices: Closing the change ticket in the tracker
questions.explanation: Production changes must be approved before they are implemented. Updating diagrams and closing the ticket happen after the change is made, and the backout plan is used only if the change fails.

questions.stem: A proposed change to the email security gateway will affect the sales, support and legal teams. Which of the following is the PRIMARY reason to identify these stakeholders before the change is approved?
choices: So the impact analysis can be skipped
So users can write the backout plan
So the maintenance window can be made much longer
So affected groups can give input and prepare
questions.answer: So affected groups can give input and prepare
questions.explanation: Identifying stakeholders lets the people affected raise concerns and plan for the change. It does not replace the impact analysis, which is still needed to assess risk.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups typically reviews requests to modify production systems and decides whether to approve or reject them?
questions.explanation: The change advisory board reviews change requests, weighs their risk and approves or rejects them. Internal audit may later check that the process was followed, but it does not approve individual changes.

questions.stem: Before approving a database patch, the change advisory board asks for evidence that the patch was installed in a staging environment that mirrors production and that all applications still worked afterward. Which of the following is the board asking for?
questions.explanation: Evidence from installing the patch in staging and checking the applications is the test results. An impact analysis estimates what could be affected, but it does not prove the patch actually works.

questions.stem: Which of the following should an impact analysis for a proposed change determine?
choices: The exact commands to run during the change
The names of the users who requested it
Which systems are affected and the risk if it fails
The purchase price of the new hardware
questions.answer: Which systems are affected and the risk if it fails
questions.explanation: An impact analysis identifies what the change could affect and how serious a failure would be. The exact commands belong in the implementation steps or procedure, not the impact analysis.

questions.stem: A patch passed every check on the developers' workstations, but the live environment includes a load balancer that those workstations do not have. After deployment, the website went down. Which of the following would MOST likely have prevented this outage?
choices: A test environment that mirrors production
A more detailed record of who owns the change
questions.answer: A test environment that mirrors production
questions.explanation: Testing is only reliable when the test environment matches production; the missing load balancer let the problem slip through. A longer maintenance window gives more time but would not have revealed the incompatibility.

questions.stem: An impact analysis shows that a proposed firewall change could block the connection to the company's payroll provider. Which of the following should the change manager do?
choices: Approve it and wait for payroll to report issues
Implement it outside the maintenance window
Remove payroll from the stakeholder list
Address the identified risk before approval
questions.answer: Address the identified risk before approval
questions.explanation: The purpose of the analysis is to find risks so they can be handled, for example by revising the rule or adding an exception, before the change is approved. Approving it anyway ignores the risk the analysis just found.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of reviewing test results during change management?
choices: Proving that every stakeholder was notified
Confirming the change works without breaking other functions
Recording which person approved the change
Choosing when the maintenance window will be
questions.answer: Confirming the change works without breaking other functions
questions.explanation: Test results show that the change does what it should and does not cause new problems. Recording who approved the change is part of the approval process, not testing.

questions.stem: A company wants every server patch to be applied the same way each time by following documented step-by-step instructions that any qualified administrator can use. Which of the following should the company create?
questions.explanation: A standard operating procedure documents repeatable steps so a task is done consistently. A backout plan only covers how to undo a change that fails, not how to perform it.

questions.stem: Which of the following should a backout plan contain?
choices: A list of stakeholders who must approve the change
The business justification for the change
Tests that prove the original problem exists
Steps to return the system to its pre-change state
questions.answer: Steps to return the system to its pre-change state
questions.explanation: A backout plan describes how to reverse the change and restore the previous working state. Business justification belongs in the change request itself.

questions.stem: A network upgrade has run past the end of its approved maintenance window, and the core switch is still not working correctly. According to typical change management policy, which of the following should the team do FIRST?
choices: Leave it as is and finish tomorrow
Ask users to stop using the network
questions.explanation: When a change fails or exceeds its approved window, the team should roll back using the backout plan to restore service. Extending the window without approval would bypass the change process.

questions.stem: Why are maintenance windows usually scheduled during periods of low system usage?
choices: To avoid the need for a backout plan
To bypass the normal approval process
To reduce the business impact of downtime
To shorten the testing phase of the change
questions.answer: To reduce the business impact of downtime
questions.explanation: Doing the work when few people use the system limits how much any outage affects the business. A backout plan is still needed because the change can fail at any time of day.

questions.stem: An administrator adds a scripting engine to the endpoint deny list. The next night, a scheduled backup job that relies on scripts fails on every server. Which of the following should have been done during change management to prevent this?
choices: Extend the maintenance window for the change
Restart the backup service after the change
Identify applications that depend on the blocked item
Store the deny list in version control
questions.answer: Identify applications that depend on the blocked item
questions.explanation: Checking dependencies would have shown that the backup job needed the scripting engine before it was blocked. Version control helps track and roll back the change but would not have revealed the dependency in advance.

questions.stem: A configuration change to the internal DNS service only takes effect after the DNS daemon is stopped and started again, which briefly stops name resolution for the whole company. Which of the following technical implications must the change plan account for?
questions.explanation: The change requires a service restart, which causes a short outage that must be planned and communicated. An allow list controls which software may run and is not involved in this change.

questions.stem: A factory runs an inventory application that is fifteen years old, is no longer supported by its vendor and is poorly documented. The team plans to upgrade the operating system beneath it. Which of the following is the MAIN risk this application presents?
choices: It will stop the board from approving the change
It will be added to the deny list automatically
It needs no testing because it has run for years
It may fail on the new system with no vendor fix
questions.answer: It may fail on the new system with no vendor fix
questions.explanation: Legacy applications often break on newer platforms, and without vendor support there may be no fix, so they need careful testing. Their age is a reason for more testing, not less.

questions.stem: A change policy states that administrators may perform only the work described in the approved change ticket. For example, they must not also update an unrelated driver while applying an approved patch. Which of the following does this policy describe?
questions.explanation: Limiting work to what was approved is a restriction on activities during the change. A maintenance window limits when the work happens, not what work is allowed.

questions.stem: An update to a web-based accounting application requires the application to be restarted. Which of the following is the MOST important reason to note this in the change plan?
choices: The restart removes the need for testing
Users may lose sessions or unsaved work
The restart replaces the backout plan
questions.answer: Users may lose sessions or unsaved work
questions.explanation: An application restart can end active sessions and discard unsaved work, so it should be scheduled and communicated. A restart does not replace testing, approval or the backout plan.

questions.stem: A planned change will take the customer portal offline for two hours. Which of the following BEST addresses this downtime as part of the change?
choices: Leave the downtime out of the documentation
Skip testing to keep the outage shorter
Turn off logging until the portal returns
Schedule it in a window and notify customers
questions.answer: Schedule it in a window and notify customers
questions.explanation: Planned downtime should be scheduled for a low-impact time and communicated to the people affected. Skipping testing to save time increases the risk that the outage lasts longer than planned.

questions.stem: After the database servers are moved to a new VLAN, which of the following documents MUST be updated so that incident responders have an accurate picture of the environment?
questions.explanation: Moving servers to a new VLAN changes the network layout, so the diagrams must be updated to match. An acceptable use policy covers how employees may use systems and is not affected by where servers sit.

questions.stem: A team changed how backups are performed but did not update the written backup procedure, which still describes the old process. Which of the following is the MOST likely risk?
choices: The change advisory board is dissolved
Staff follow outdated steps during a recovery
Encryption keys are rotated too often
questions.answer: Staff follow outdated steps during a recovery
questions.explanation: If the procedure no longer matches reality, people who rely on it during a stressful recovery may perform the wrong steps. Outdated documentation does not affect backup speed or key rotation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a PRIMARY security benefit of keeping infrastructure configuration files in a version control system?
choices: Encryption of the files while they are stored
A history of each change with the option to roll back
questions.answer: A history of each change with the option to roll back
questions.explanation: Version control records who changed what and when, and it lets the team return to an earlier version. It does not by itself stop unauthorized changes or replace the approval process.

questions.stem: A change has been implemented and tested successfully. Which of the following should be the FINAL step in the change process?
choices: Update documentation to reflect the change
Submit the change request for review
Perform an impact analysis of the change
Obtain approval from the change board
questions.answer: Update documentation to reflect the change
questions.explanation: Once a change is in place and verified, the documentation is updated so it matches the new state. Submitting the request, analyzing impact and getting approval all happen before implementation.

questions.stem: A team changed the firewall to allow two new ports but the documented firewall standard still lists only the old set of allowed ports. An auditor finds the mismatch. Which of the following change management steps was missed?
questions.explanation: After a change, related policies and procedures must be updated so they match how systems are actually configured. The mismatch is a documentation gap; it says nothing about whether an impact analysis was done.

questions.stem: In a public key infrastructure, which of the following must be kept secret by its owner and never shared?
questions.explanation: The private key proves the owner's identity and decrypts data sent to them, so it must stay secret. The public key and certificate are designed to be shared freely.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the relationship between the two keys in an asymmetric key pair?
choices: Both keys are identical and held by both parties
Data encrypted with one key is decrypted with the other
The private key is published and the public one hidden
Either key can easily be calculated from the other
questions.answer: Data encrypted with one key is decrypted with the other
questions.explanation: In asymmetric cryptography, what one key of the pair encrypts only the other key can decrypt. Identical keys held by both parties describe symmetric encryption, not asymmetric.

questions.stem: A company wants to issue each employee a certificate that ties the employee's identity to a cryptographic key, manage those certificates centrally and be able to revoke them. Which of the following should the company implement?
questions.explanation: A PKI provides certificate authorities, issuance, and revocation for binding identities to public keys. A symmetric key exchange only creates shared keys and does not issue or revoke identity certificates.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY security concern with using key escrow?
choices: The escrow holder becomes a valuable target
Escrowed keys can no longer encrypt data
Key escrow makes keys shorter and weaker
Escrow prevents data from being recovered
questions.answer: The escrow holder becomes a valuable target
questions.explanation: Because the escrow holder keeps copies of keys, compromising it could expose many keys at once, so it must be strongly protected. Escrow exists to make recovery possible, so the option saying it prevents recovery is the opposite of its purpose.

questions.stem: A company needs to encrypt several terabytes of backup data each night as quickly as possible. Which of the following is the BEST choice?
questions.explanation: Symmetric algorithms such as AES are much faster than asymmetric ones, which makes them suited to large amounts of data. Asymmetric encryption is too slow for bulk data and is mainly used for key exchange and signatures.

questions.stem: A clinic wants each patient's entry in its database to be encrypted with a separate key, so that if one key is exposed, only that one patient's data is at risk. Which of the following levels of encryption does this describe?
questions.explanation: Encrypting each record individually limits the damage from a single key to one record. Transparent database encryption protects the whole database with one key, so exposing that key exposes every patient.

questions.stem: A mobile banking app sends account data to the bank's servers, and customers often use public Wi-Fi. Which of the following BEST protects the data from eavesdroppers on the same network?
questions.explanation: Transport encryption, such as TLS, protects data while it travels across the network. Database encryption protects data stored on the server and does nothing for data in transit.

questions.stem: An auditor finds that a legacy site-to-site VPN still uses DES with a 56-bit key. Which of the following is the BEST recommendation?
choices: Run DES twice with the same key
Hash the DES key with MD5
questions.explanation: A 56-bit key is short enough to brute-force, so the VPN should move to a modern algorithm with a longer key, such as AES-256. Running DES twice with the same key adds little strength and keeps the weak algorithm.

questions.stem: Several people share a laptop. One user needs a single spreadsheet to be encrypted while all other files on the laptop remain accessible to everyone. Which of the following BEST meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: File-level encryption protects just the chosen file and leaves everything else untouched. Full-disk encryption protects the entire drive but, once the system is unlocked, does not keep one file private from other users.

questions.stem: A company runs dozens of cloud applications that each use encryption keys. It wants a managed service that centrally creates, rotates and stores keys, applies access policies to them and logs every use. Which of the following BEST meets this need?
questions.explanation: A key management system handles the full key lifecycle, including creation, rotation, access control and auditing, across many applications. A key escrow agent only holds copies of keys for recovery and does not create, rotate or police their use, and a Trusted Platform Module is a chip in one computer and cannot manage keys for many cloud applications.

questions.stem: A smartphone processes fingerprint data in an isolated area of its main processor that the operating system cannot access, even if the operating system is compromised. Which of the following is this isolated area?
questions.explanation: A secure enclave is a protected, isolated area within the processor that keeps sensitive operations away from the main operating system. A TPM is a separate chip, typically on a computer's motherboard, rather than an isolated area of the main processor.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the difference between a hardware security module (HSM) and a Trusted Platform Module (TPM)?
choices: An HSM is a dedicated device for heavy key use; a TPM is a chip in one computer
An HSM stores certificates only; a TPM issues certificates to users
An HSM is software-based; a TPM is a cloud service for many systems
An HSM hashes passwords; a TPM encrypts network traffic
questions.answer: An HSM is a dedicated device for heavy key use; a TPM is a chip in one computer
questions.explanation: An HSM is a dedicated, often network-attached appliance built for high-volume key generation and storage, while a TPM is a chip on one device's motherboard that protects that device's keys and boot integrity. Neither is a software or cloud-only service, which rules out that option.

questions.stem: Call center agents verify customers by asking for the last four digits of their card number. The agents' screens display card numbers as ****-****-****-1234. Which of the following techniques is being used?
questions.explanation: Hiding most of a value while showing a part of it is data masking. Tokenization replaces the entire value with a substitute token, so no real digits would be shown.

questions.stem: Which of the following obfuscation techniques hides the very existence of a message by embedding it inside another file, such as an audio recording?
questions.explanation: Steganography conceals data inside an ordinary-looking carrier file so that no one suspects a message is there. Data masking hides parts of a value but does not hide the fact that the data exists.

questions.stem: Developers need realistic customer data in a test environment, but real names and phone numbers must not be exposed. The test data will never need to be converted back to the original values. Which of the following is the BEST approach?
questions.explanation: Masking replaces sensitive values with realistic but fake ones, which is ideal when the originals never need to be recovered. Tokenization is designed to be reversible through a token vault, which adds complexity the test environment does not need.

questions.stem: A mobile payment wallet stores a substitute value on the phone instead of the real card number. The substitute is useless if stolen, and only the payment network can map it back to the real card. Which of the following techniques does this describe?
questions.explanation: Replacing a sensitive value with a token that can be mapped back only through a secure system is tokenization. Data masking hides part of a value for display and is not meant to be mapped back to the original for transactions.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes a cryptographic hash function?
choices: A reversible function that uses a shared key
A one-way function with a fixed-length output
A function whose output matches the input length
A two-way function that uses a key pair
questions.answer: A one-way function with a fixed-length output
questions.explanation: A hash function turns input of any size into a fixed-length digest that cannot practically be reversed. A reversible function with a shared key describes symmetric encryption, not hashing.

questions.stem: A company signs its software updates before releasing them. Which of the following does the digital signature provide for customers who verify it?
questions.explanation: Verifying the signature shows the update has not been altered and came from the holder of the signing key, who cannot deny signing it. A signature does not encrypt the update, so it provides no confidentiality.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a key stretching algorithm used to protect stored passwords?
questions.explanation: bcrypt applies many rounds of hashing to slow down brute-force attacks, which is key stretching. MD5 is a fast hash function, and speed is exactly what makes it a poor choice for storing passwords.

questions.stem: Which of the following features of a blockchain makes it difficult to change a transaction after it has been recorded?
choices: Each block includes the hash of the previous block
Each block is encrypted with a single shared AES key
A central administrator approves every edit
All blocks are stored on a single server
questions.answer: Each block includes the hash of the previous block
questions.explanation: Because each block contains the previous block's hash, changing an old block breaks every link after it, which other participants would detect. A blockchain does not rely on a central administrator; it is decentralized.

questions.stem: Cryptocurrency transactions are recorded in a shared record that anyone can view and verify, even though participants are identified only by addresses. Which of the following BEST describes this record?
questions.explanation: An open public ledger is a record that anyone can read and verify, which is how public blockchains work. A permissioned database limits who can see and verify entries, so it is not open.

questions.stem: Several suppliers in a supply chain want to confirm the origin and handling history of each shipment without depending on any single company to keep the records. Which of the following technologies BEST meets this need?
questions.explanation: A blockchain gives all participants a shared, tamper-evident record that no single party controls. A certificate authority is a central trusted party, which is exactly what the suppliers want to avoid depending on.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY reason a distributed ledger resists tampering by a single participant?
choices: Many participants hold copies and must agree on changes
All entries are encrypted with one master key
Only the entry's creator is able to read it
Entries are deleted once they have been verified
questions.answer: Many participants hold copies and must agree on changes
questions.explanation: Because many independent participants keep copies and must reach consensus, one participant cannot quietly rewrite history. A single master key would create a central weakness, which is the opposite of how a distributed ledger works.

questions.stem: A certificate authority publishes a signed file, updated on a schedule, that names the serial numbers of certificates it has invalidated before their expiration dates. Which of the following is this file?
questions.explanation: A certificate revocation list is the published list of revoked certificate serial numbers. OCSP also checks revocation, but it answers a query about one certificate at a time rather than publishing a full list.

questions.stem: A browser trusts a bank's website certificate because the certificate chains up to a certificate already installed in the browser's trust store. Which of the following is that pre-installed certificate?
questions.explanation: The root CA certificate in the trust store is the root of trust that every certificate in the chain leads back to. An intermediate CA certificate sits between the root and the website and is usually sent by the server, not pre-installed.

questions.stem: An employee reports that the laptop holding the private key for their email signing certificate was stolen. Which of the following should the administrator do FIRST?
choices: Renew the certificate with the same key
Convert it to a wildcard certificate
questions.explanation: Revoking the certificate tells relying parties to stop trusting anything signed with the stolen key. Renewing with the same key would keep the compromised key in use.
